comments.body:
# RCA — Phase 1 complete. The effect is REAL, but `nohup` is not the cause.

Investigated in an isolated worktree off `origin/main` (`987caf8c73`), `tests/e2e/js` warmed
(`npm install` + `npm run build`), Chromium verified launching. Machine load average 9-13
throughout (this host runs several agents), i.e. the contention the ticket names as a candidate
was present in every run below.

## Finding 1 — detachment ALONE does not reproduce it (0 / 15 runs)

Exact invocations, both from the same worktree:

    # foreground
    env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest \
      tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py -q

    # detached, stdin at /dev/null, no controlling terminal (as reported)
    nohup env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest \
      tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py -q \
      > /tmp/log 2>&1 < /dev/null &

Results:
- foreground, 7-test subset: **7 passed / 22.6s**
- detached, same subset: **7 passed / 22.7s** (identical)
- detached, full 12-test selection, N=6 consecutive: **12 passed every time**
  (27.9 / 28.6 / 26.9 / 27.8 / 27.x / 27.x s)
- detached `pytest tests/e2e` (warm): **12 passed** — the exact number the report cites
- three CONCURRENT detached `pytest tests/e2e` + one `test_reclaim_bridge_history.py`,
  3 rounds (8 e2e runs + 2 integration runs, uninterfered): **all clean, 0 failures**

So the absent TTY, `stdin=/dev/null`, the process session, and resource contention are all
**rejected** as causes. "Detached runs are untrustworthy" is not a property of detachment.

Also worth recording, because it makes the cold path safe: with `tests/e2e/js/node_modules`
absent (the state of a FRESH worktree, which `AGENTS.md` mandates), `pytest tests/e2e` reports
**4 passed, 8 skipped** — the tier self-skips, exactly as `tests/e2e/conftest.py`'s module
docstring promises. It does not error.

## Finding 2 — the mechanism that DOES reproduce it: a concurrent external mutation of the
## shared checkout, misattributed by an autouse guard to an innocent test

`tests/conftest.py:297-325` `_no_repo_root_leaks` is an autouse fixture that snapshots the
top-level entries of `REPO_ROOT` before each test and diffs them after. It cannot tell an
in-test mutation from an external one.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT (deterministic, 1/1):

    # detached run of the implicated integration file; from a separate shell,
    # 4s in, a single external touch — nothing the tests do:
    touch /Users/joeoakhart/debug-f0fb-detached-pytest/EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE

Observed:

    E  Failed: Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT (use tmp_path or a sandboxed temp dir):
       ['EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE']
    tests/conftest.py:322: Failed
    ERROR tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py::test_cli_never_invokes_push_and_leaves_source_refs_exact
    6 passed, 1 error in 7.55s

Three things to note, all of which match the original report exactly:

1. **`6 passed, 1 error`** — the guard fires in TEARDOWN, so the test still counts as passed
   AND raises an error. "It errored, then on re-run the file's 6 passed" is not two
   contradictory observations; it is one run reporting both. (Verified independently with a
   throwaway autouse teardown-fail fixture: pytest renders it `1 passed, 1 error`.)
2. **It blamed an innocent test.** `test_cli_never_invokes_push_and_leaves_source_refs_exact`
   did nothing wrong. The guard attributes to whichever test happened to straddle the external
   write — arbitrary, and different on each run. Same signature the HEAD-move sibling has.
3. **The message asserts a falsehood** — "Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT" — when no
   test leaked anything. And the guard **deleted the external file** (`tests/conftest.py:316`
   `target.unlink()`): the probe was gone afterwards. A detached suite will silently delete a
   new top-level file an agent creates while it runs.

## Finding 3 — the second mechanism: a signal-killed child probe reports NO cause at all

The report's own session records "tests/interfaces clean through 59% before **the runner was
reaped**". Reaping is therefore established for that session. What a reap does to the browser
tier (deterministic, 4/4 — `kill -9` on the `node` probe child mid-test):

    E  AssertionError: browser_diag.mjs produced no output; stderr:
    tests/e2e/conftest.py:106: AssertionError

`tests/e2e/conftest.py:100-109` raises on empty stdout and prints `proc.stderr` — which is
EMPTY when the child died on a signal — and **never inspects `proc.returncode`** (it is `-9`
here). The resulting message names no cause whatsoever, and is indistinguishable from a real
product regression. That is precisely why the reporter "nearly chased those as real
regressions".

Note this also matters for `nohup`: `nohup` ignores SIGHUP but does NOT `setsid`. Measured on
this host, a `nohup ... &` child has the SAME pgid as the launching shell, so every `git` and
`node` subprocess these fixtures spawn is reapable by one `kill -- -PGID`.

## Why this looked like "detached vs foreground"

Both mechanisms need an EXTERNAL actor running concurrently with the suite. A foreground run
structurally prevents that — the agent is blocked waiting on it. A detached run exists
precisely so the agent can keep working in the same checkout, so it is the only mode in which
a concurrent `git commit`, branch switch, file creation, or reap can land mid-run. Detachment
is an ENABLER of the real cause, not the cause. That distinction is the whole ticket: the
remedy is not "distrust detached runs", it is "do not mutate the checkout while a suite runs
in it, and make the guards say so when someone does".

## Separating this from the KNOWN self-inflicted HEAD-move class (AC3)

They are siblings, not the same thing, and both are external-mutation misattributions:
- `_no_repo_commits` (`tests/conftest.py:610-633`) — "Test moved the repo HEAD (X -> Y)".
  Already understood; fires on a concurrent commit/rebase/branch switch.
- `_no_repo_root_leaks` (`tests/conftest.py:297-325`) — "Test leaked new entries into
  REPO_ROOT". The one this report actually hit, and the one that had NOT been named. It fires
  on any concurrent top-level write, and additionally DELETES what it finds.

The reason the report read as a new mystery is that only the HEAD-move sibling was folklore.
A real precedent for the leak guard exists in a detached full-suite log on this host from the
previous day: `14671 passed, 55 skipped, 4 errors in 1:10:59`, all four errors
`Failed: Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT`, on four unrelated unit tests.

## Prior art — this guard firing on a NON-TEST cause is already a filed-and-fixed bug class

- `3a03-9863-542e-4ae1` (`hurt-brow-swan`, closed) — `_no_repo_root_leaks` blind to leaks into
  pre-existing top-level dirs.
- `f8a2-bf40-4cc4-479b` (`dizzy-splice-coven`, closed) — "bash-suite REPO_ROOT leak
  (.tickets-tracker) + **macOS tmp-cleaner race**". A non-test external actor tripping this
  guard, filed and fixed as a bug.
- Ticket `5ac8` records another: "1 environmental teardown artifact (.tickets-tracker symlink
  flagged by the REPO_ROOT leak detector ...; the test passes in isolation".

So "the leak guard reports an environmental cause as a test defect" is established in this
project as a defect, not as intended behaviour.

## Defect origin (`caused_by`) — UNATTRIBUTABLE, with the searches

The implicated lines are the `pytest.fail` message and the `unlink`/`rmtree` cleanup,
`tests/conftest.py:311-325`. `git blame -w -C -M -L 305,325` puts all of them on
**`b534f47a7f9`** (2026-06-08), "Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone
rebar" — the commit that first added `tests/conftest.py`
(`git log --diff-filter=A -- tests/conftest.py` returns only that commit). It carries **no
`rebar-ticket:` trailer** (only a `Co-Authored-By:`); it predates the trailer convention.

Date test: the guard has behaved this way since the file's first commit, so this is an
OMISSION (it was never written to consider a concurrent external mutator), not a regression —
there is no commit that made it wrong. Tracker searches for the originating work
(`rebar search "repo isolation guard leak REPO_ROOT"`, `rebar search "local-dev-env whole tree
validation detached"`) return only later bugs ABOUT the guard (`3a03`, `f8a2`), not the work
that introduced it. Recording as **unattributable** rather than charging it to the mass
extraction import or to one of the later bugs that merely widened it.

## What is left, and why it is an OPERATOR DECISION rather than something I landed

AC5 as written ("if specific tests genuinely cannot run detached, they SKIP") rests on a
premise this investigation DISPROVES: no test here is unable to run detached — all 15 detached
runs were clean. Adding a skip keyed on detachment would suppress a signal for a cause that
does not exist, which is the "erosion of the signal" this ticket was filed to prevent.

The remedies the evidence actually supports, none of which I applied unilaterally because each
changes a safety guard or the project's documented method:

1. **`docs/local-dev-env.md` (AC4) — a genuine, verified gap.** `grep -rn -i
   'nohup|detached|background'` over `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `Makefile`
   returns ZERO hits. The detached-suite practice is entirely undocumented folklore. The
   recorded guidance should be: detached runs ARE trustworthy, provided nothing else touches
   the checkout while they run; run them from a DEDICATED worktree; and prefer
   `-n <cores> --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread -p no:cacheprovider
   --basetemp=...` (what CI uses — `pytest-xdist` and `pytest-timeout` are already pinned in
   `[dev]` for local<->CI parity but are NOT enabled by `addopts`, so a bare local run is
   serial with no hang guard).
2. **`tests/conftest.py:322-325`** — stop asserting "Test leaked"; say the entry MAY come from
   a concurrent process outside the test, and name that possibility. Purely additive to the
   message; weakens no detection.
3. **`tests/conftest.py:310-321`** — reconsider deleting entries the guard cannot attribute.
   Today a detached suite destroys a concurrent agent's new top-level file.
4. **`tests/e2e/conftest.py:106-109`** — include `proc.returncode` in the diagnostic. A `-9`
   or `-15` tells a reader instantly that the child was killed rather than that the product
   broke. Additive; changes no pass/fail outcome.

(2) and (4) are additive-diagnostic and low risk. (3) genuinely weakens a cleanup that exists
for a reason. (1) is the ticket's headline deliverable. All four want an operator's call on
scope before they land, so I am stopping Phase 1 here rather than patching a safety guard on
my own judgement.

# Phase 2 complete — Gerrit 1964

Scope per operator direction: land (1) the docs gap, (2) the leak-guard message, (4) the
e2e returncode diagnostic. The deletion behaviour (3) was explicitly NOT touched; it stays
with `746c-185a-0e48-4b83` (`carryable-basalt-beagle`), which now carries this
investigation's deterministic reproduction as a comment and is linked `relates_to`.

## Plan re-review

AC5's premise was disproven by the investigation, so the description was corrected rather
than closed against a refuted criterion: AC5 now asserts that NO detachment-keyed skip is
introduced (with the measured result inline), and two new criteria cover the honest guard
message and the returncode diagnostic. `set-file-impact` recorded the 6 real paths, and
`rebar review-plan` re-earned the attestation: **verdict PASS, blocking [], signed**
(`verified_at_sha ac3f6c1e60`). Three advisories, all below their block thresholds and left
as-is — the strongest is that the pre-investigation "Candidate mechanisms" framing still
reads as if the browser/TTY lead were live; the RCA comment above reconciles it, and
re-editing the description would only re-stale the signature just earned.

## RED -> GREEN

Oracle: `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py` (4 tests).

- Seams were created FIRST, behaviour-preserving (`tests/_isolation.py::leak_failure_message`,
  new `tests/_child_diag.py::child_failure_detail`), so the oracle could fail on ASSERTIONS
  rather than on an import.
- **RED, for the right reason.** 3 assertion failures, including
  `AssertionError: assert '-9' in 'stderr:\n'` — the killed child's stderr is literally
  empty, which is the reported signature reproduced inside a unit test.
- The oracle was then **moved out of the worktree** and the fix implemented by a subagent
  given only the frozen contract — it never saw the test file or its assertions.
- **GREEN** on re-applying the held-out oracle: 16 passed (the 4 new + the existing
  `test_repo_isolation_guard.py` suite).
- **Mutation check, both mechanisms, anchors asserted applied.** Re-introducing the exact
  confirmed defects (drop `proc.returncode`; restore "Test leaked new entries into
  REPO_ROOT") returned the oracle to **RED, 3 failed**. Restored, green again.
- **Refactoring litmus:** every assertion is on a pure function's returned string — no
  private names, no source greps — so a rename or an extraction cannot redden it.

## Replication of the original report

Through the real entry point, with the fix in place: `kill -9` on the `node` browser probe
mid-test now reports

    AssertionError: browser_diag.mjs produced no output; child was killed by SIGKILL
    (returncode -9) — some external process killed it rather than it failing on its own;
    a detached run sharing this checkout may have been reaped; stderr was empty

against the previous `browser_diag.mjs produced no output; stderr:` followed by nothing.
The failure mode that made the 1943 agent "nearly chase those as real regressions" is gone:
the message now names the external cause.

An unplanned live confirmation also occurred mid-session. A concurrent `make typecheck`
created `.mypy_cache` while the suite was running, and the new guard text reported it
correctly as `New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.mypy_cache']` rather
than accusing the test. That is the bug happening in the wild, caught by the fix.

## Gates and regressions

`make lint` exit 0; `make typecheck` exit 0 (598 files);
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` -> `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
Regression: full `tests/e2e` tier **12 passed** with the changed conftest.

## Scope and safety

- **Caller-dependency sweep: clear.** No test pins either message string (`grep` for
  "leaked new entries" and "produced no output" across `tests/` and `src/`); the only
  matches were the definitions themselves and unrelated assertions that already check
  `returncode`.
- **Restoration, not creation.** No new entry point, command, or user-visible artifact; both
  changes only add information to an existing failure message.
- **No new dependency.** `signal` is stdlib.
- **No test weakened.** No assertion removed or loosened, no skip/xfail added; detection is
  unchanged in both guards — only the wording is.

## Sibling sweep (Step 7)

**Construct axis** — other sites raising on a child's stderr without consulting its
returncode. Both `tests/e2e/conftest.py` sites fixed in scope (the `bpmn_harness` one at the
old line 64 had the identical defect and was routed through the same helper). Confirmed
sibling NOT fixed in scope, filed as **`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`** (`obvious-saline-gerbil`):
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` has 17+ `assert "Traceback" not in
cp.stderr` sites which **fail OPEN** on a signal-killed child (empty stderr satisfies the
assertion) — the same missing-returncode construct in the opposite, more dangerous
direction. Left out of scope because the `external` tier needs live Jira DC credentials, so
it cannot be validated by this change's RED->GREEN path. Not siblings on inspection:
`test_authorship_fixture_maintenance.py:60` and `test_attestation_signing.py:486` already
assert on `returncode`; `test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:56` subclasses
`CalledProcessError`, whose `__str__` already reports the signal.

**Parity axis** — the rule is "a whole-checkout state guard must not assert the test caused
what it cannot attribute". Census of the surfaces that apply that rule:
`_no_repo_root_leaks` (fixed here); `_no_repo_commits` — **MISSING**, filed as
**`ca58-bc06-59eb-49f8`** (`unfair-dopey-kakapo`): its message asserts "it committed into
the rebar checkout" and prescribes `git reset --hard`, both false and the latter destructive
when the HEAD move came from a concurrent external commit. Deliberately not fixed here
because this ticket scopes the HEAD-move class out as separately known, and the operator
scoped this change to (1)(2)(4). The session-finish porcelain backstop reports without
attributing to a test — N/A. Both siblings are linked `discovered_from` this bug.

## Residual risk

- **Accepted:** the guards still cannot ATTRIBUTE an entry, only describe both possibilities.
  Real attribution is the open design question on `746c`.
- **Ticket filed:** the two siblings above.
- **Fixed in scope:** the two diagnostics and the docs gap.

## Attribution

Unchanged and deliberate: **unattributable**, with the searches recorded in the RCA comment
above. The implicated lines trace to `b534f47a7f9`, the commit that first added
`tests/conftest.py`, which carries no `rebar-ticket:` trailer (it predates the convention);
the date test shows an omission rather than a regression, so no commit made it wrong. No
guessed `--caused-by` will be passed on the close.

## Report — NOT independently reproduced yet, read the caveat
An agent landing Gerrit 1943 reported that running pytest **detached via `nohup`** produced errors
that **did not reproduce in a foreground shell**:

- two bpmn-io browser e2e tests, and
- `test_partial_clone_refusal_names_fresh_unfiltered_clone_remedy`

all errored under the detached run, then **passed on a foreground re-run** (12 passed / 6 passed).
It recorded that it "nearly chased those as real regressions."

**I have not reproduced this myself.** This ticket is filed to establish whether the effect is real
and what causes it — not to assert a defect. Investigation should start by reproducing the
foreground/detached difference on an unmodified tree before touching anything.

## Why it is worth establishing rather than shrugging off
Agents in this project routinely run the full suite detached, because a serial local run takes hours
and exceeds tool timeouts. If a detached run reports errors a foreground run does not, then the
cheap validation path produces false positives, and the expensive path is the only trustworthy one.
Two costs follow:

1. **Wasted investigation.** At least one agent nearly root-caused phantom regressions. Time spent
   chasing an artifact is time not spent on the actual change.
2. **Erosion of the signal.** The dangerous direction is the inverse of (1): once "errors in the
   detached run are probably spurious" becomes folklore, a REAL regression in a detached run gets
   waved through with the same shrug. That is the same failure mode the withdrawn ticket
   `bitesized-fluorite-aruanas` warned about for `tests/interfaces` — dismissing a class of failure
   by reputation rather than by diagnosis.

## Distinguish this from a KNOWN and different artifact
Several agents this session reported errors in long background runs that were **self-inflicted and
fully explained**: the run raced the agent's own `git commit` / `git reset --hard` / branch switch in
the same worktree, and repo-hygiene guards fired with messages naming the exact HEAD move (e.g.
"Test moved the repo HEAD (a9cbc2d34e -> 74daf58e52)"). Those are not this. They are correct guards
catching a genuinely mutating tree.

The report here is different in kind: no HEAD move was implicated, and the same commit passed
foreground. Investigation must not conflate the two — establishing which of the reported errors
belong to which class is itself part of the work.

## Candidate mechanisms to discriminate between
- Process-group / TTY differences under `nohup` (browser e2e tests in particular may need a session
  or display that a detached process lacks).
- Working-directory or environment differences between the detached process and the foreground shell.
- Resource contention: a detached full-tree run may overlap other work in a way a foreground run does
  not, hitting timeouts that read as errors.
- Harness reaping: a detached runner being partially killed and its teardown reported as errors.

The bpmn-io **browser** e2e tests are the strongest lead — a browser harness is exactly the kind of
thing that behaves differently without a controlling terminal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The foreground/detached difference is either REPRODUCED on an unmodified tree, or shown not to
      reproduce — with the exact invocations for both runs recorded so a later reader can repeat them.
- [x] If it reproduces, each affected test is classified: genuinely environment-dependent (and why),
      versus a real defect the detached run exposes. Do not stop at "spurious."
- [x] The reported errors are separated from the KNOWN self-inflicted HEAD-move class, so the two are
      not conflated in whatever guidance results.
- [x] Whatever the outcome, the recommended way for an agent to validate the whole tree locally is
      recorded in `docs/local-dev-env.md` — including whether detached runs are trustworthy, and if
      not, what to do instead given a serial run exceeds tool timeouts.
- [x] No detachment-keyed skip is introduced. **Investigation result (2026-08-20): the original
      premise of this criterion is DISPROVEN.** No test here is unable to run detached — 15 detached
      runs at load average 9-13, with `stdin=/dev/null` and no controlling terminal, were entirely
      clean, including `pytest tests/e2e` reporting the same `12 passed` the report cites. The
      failures are caused by a **concurrent external actor mutating the shared checkout** while the
      suite runs (proven deterministically), not by detachment; detachment is only the mode in which
      such an actor can exist, because a foreground run blocks the agent that would otherwise be
      mutating the checkout. A skip keyed on detachment would therefore suppress a real signal for a
      cause that does not exist — precisely the "erosion of the signal" this ticket was filed to
      prevent. This criterion is met by NOT adding such a skip, and by the diagnostics instead being
      made honest about the external-actor cause (see the two criteria below).
- [x] `tests/conftest.py`'s REPO_ROOT leak-guard message no longer asserts that a test leaked an
      entry it may not have created; it names the concurrent-external-process possibility. Additive
      to the message only — no detection is weakened, and the deletion behaviour is deliberately NOT
      touched here (it is owned by `746c-185a-0e48-4b83`, `carryable-basalt-beagle`).
- [x] The `tests/e2e` browser-probe failure diagnostic reports the child's `returncode`, so a
      signal-killed child (a reaped detached run) is distinguishable at a glance from a genuine
      product failure. Additive; changes no pass/fail outcome.

## Provenance
Reported 2026-08-20 by the agent on ticket `visionary-pernicious-ynambu` (Gerrit 1943, merged), which
recorded it as a method note rather than absorbing it. Filed here so it is investigated rather than
becoming folklore.

file_impact.reason: AC4: record how to validate the whole tree locally, whether detached runs are trustworthy (yes, from a worktree nothing else touches), the CI flags, and how to read a guard error
add leak_failure_message(): the REPO_ROOT leak guard text, no longer asserting the test leaked; names the concurrent-external-writer cause
_no_repo_root_leaks calls the shared message builder instead of inlining the false assertion
new shared helper child_failure_detail(): reports a child returncode and signal name so a reaped run is distinguishable from a product failure
both harness/browser probe raise sites report the child returncode via the shared helper instead of an empty stderr
new held-out RED->GREEN oracle for both diagnostics, incl. a real SIGKILLed child

compiled_state.title: Detached (nohup) pytest runs report errors that do not reproduce in a foreground shell
